text:
customer_jones: Hey team — after upgrading to @redwood/ts-sdk@0.23 our embedding calls are 404ing. Error from node: "Error: 404 Unknown route: /v1/embeddings.create". Happening in prod after deployment a few minutes ago. Anyone seen this?

sasha_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the minimal call you made and the exact SDK version + node runtime?

customer_jones: Node 18.16.0, ts-sdk 0.23.0. Minimal repro:```js
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/ts-sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'open-embed-large', input: ['hello'] })
```
Error stack: `Error: 404 Unknown route: /v1/embeddings.create`

sasha_support: thanks — that helps. Two quick asks: 1) can you try against the REST path directly with curl (to confirm SDK vs API)? 2) does pinning @redwood/ts-sdk@0.22 work as a temporary rollback?

customer_jones: curl to REST path returns same 404:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings.create \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-large","input":["hello"]}'
# -> {"error":"Unknown route: /v1/embeddings.create"}
```
We rolled back to ts-sdk 0.22 and calls succeed.

sasha_support: good repro, thanks. escalating to eng — @devon_engineering can you take a look? sounds like a route rename or canary mismatch. :eyes:

ci-deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed for api-service (release/2026.03.16) at 2026-03-16T14:12:04Z

devon_engineering: taking it. quick triage: we shipped a small API surface change in canary earlier that renamed some RPC-style endpoints to RESTy names (e.g. `/v1/embeddings.create` -> `/v1/embeddings`) and added param rename `model` -> `model_name` in the new handler. looks like some customers hit the canary traffic.

alex_prod: confirming — canary diff shows handler route change and new strict path matching. fallback shim wasn't applied to canary nodes.

devon_engineering: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback canary (ops), 2) apply shim on API gateway to support old route names for 24–48h, 3) quick SDK patch returning to older route names (published 0.23.1 hotfix). Ops, can you roll back canary while we prepare shim?

alex_prod: ops rolled back canary at 14:20 UTC. Most traffic back to stable nodes.

customer_jones: thanks — after rollback our traffic is fine again with ts-sdk 0.23? or should we keep on 0.22?

devon_engineering: after rollback stable API still supports old routes. 0.23 will work once we re-release canary with the shim. we will also publish a small SDK patch that tolerates both param names for a short window.

customer_jones: appreciate the quick follow-up. one more thing — we saw repeated retries from our service which spiked token usage while the 404s happened. any advice for retry backoff until this is resolved?

sasha_support: recommend exponential backoff + 429/5xx only; treat 404 Unknown route as a non-transient error for now (no retries). If you need a rule: retry on >=500 or network errs with base backoff 200ms, multiplier 2, max 5 attempts.

devon_engineering: internal action items: - create hotfix branch r/ts-sdk-0.23-route-shim - publish 0.23.1 that maps `embeddings.create` -> `embeddings` and accepts both `model` and `model_name` keys - add api-gateway shim on canary and stable - add automated smoke check that runs simple embeddings + chat endpoints post-deploy.

sasha_support: I'll follow up with the customer when 0.23.1 is published and when gateway shim is live.

customer_jones: thanks all — please ping when the SDK patch is out. :thumbsup:

devon_engineering: quick repro note for the team (for the ticket): sample failing error body from SDK: `{"status":404,"message":"Unknown route: /v1/embeddings.create","code":"route_not_found"}`. Also noticed auth header was fine — token validated on rollback.

ci-deploy-bot: Patch release 0.23.1 published for @redwood/ts-sdk at 2026-03-16T15:02:11Z (contains route compatibility shim)

sasha_support: 0.23.1 published. @customer_jones can you try `npm i @redwood/ts-sdk@0.23.1` and confirm?

customer_jones: installing now... ✅ calls succeed with 0.23.1. No more 404s. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

sasha_support: great — closing the incident on our side, will follow up with postmortem notes & release checklist changes. :white_check_mark:
